chapter_title_ka: სამთაგანვე ქვაბსა მისლვა და მუნით არაბეთს წასლვა
chapter_title_en: Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia
chapter_expert_explanation_en: The three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. Tariel sends Asmat ahead and personally intercedes with King Rostevan to pardon Avtandil for his secret departure and bless Avtandil's marriage to Queen Tinatin.

ღმერთი კარგსა მოავლინებს და ბოროტსა არ დაბადებს

stanzas.english_translation: This hidden thing Divnos the sage reveals: "God sends good, He creates no evil, He shortens the bad to a moment, He renews (? repeats) the good continuously (? for a long time), His perfect self He makes more perfect, He degrades not Himself."

stanzas.english_translation: Those lions, those suns, set out from P’hridon's (country). They lead with them the sun-faced, the maiden, the amazing to beholders; the raven's tail (of her hair), ordered, hangs coiled by the crystal (of her brow or cheek); beauty, tenderness, there adorned the (fine) ruby.

stanzas.english_translation: That sun sat in a palanquin, and thus they made her fare. They followed the chase; there caused they blood to flow. Wherever they came upon a land they were the joy of beholders, they went forth to meet them, gave gifts, eulogized, reviled them not.

stanzas.english_translation: It was as if the sun sat in the firmament amid moons. Many days they journeyed, merry, sagely discoursing, within those great plains on all sides unattained of men. They reached the neighbourhood of that rock where Tariel had been.

stanzas.english_translation: Tariel said: "It is seemly that I should be your host this day. Thither will I go where I was while madness afflicted me. There will Asmat’h entertain us; she hath (store of) smoked meat. When I give you fair gifts you shall praise the variety of the treasure."

ასმათს უც ხორცი ირმისა, იქმს მასპინძლობა-კვეთასა.

stanzas.english_translation: They went in; they dismounted in that cave of the great rocks. Asmat’h had venison; she carves it for the guests. They were merry, they joked at the passing of those deeds; they thanked God that He had turned their. days of woe to joy.

პოვნეს იგი საჭურჭლენი, ტარიასგან დაბეჭდულნი,

stanzas.english_translation: They explored the hollow hill, merry they played; they found those treasures sealed up by Taria, uncounted by any, apprehended by none; they say not with dissatisfied hearts: "We lack!"

უბოძა ტურფა მრავალი მათ მათი შესადარები.
კვლა ფრიდონისნი აავსნა, სპა ჰყვა თუ სპასალარები,
აივსო კაცი ყველაი მაშინ მათ თანა ნარები,

stanzas.english_translation: He gave many fair gifts, to each what was fitting; then he enriched P’hridon's people, army and generals alike; every man was enriched, (all) those who came with them, but there lay so much treasure it seemed still untouched by man.

ფრიდონს უთხრა: “ვალი თქვენი ჩემგან ძნელად გარდიხდების,
მაგრა თქმულა: «კარგის მქმნელი კაცი ბოლოდ არ წახდების»;
აწ საჭურჭლე რაზომიცა აქა ძეს და ან იდების,

stanzas.english_translation: He said to P’hridon: "Hard will it be for me to pay the debt I owe thee; but it is said: 'A man who is a doer of good loseth not in the end.' Now the treasure, as much as lieth here or is to be found, let it all be thine, take it away, as it belongs to thee." so

ფრიდონ მდაბლად თაყვანი სცა,ჰკადრა მადლი მეტის-მეტი:
“მე, მეფეო, რად გგონივარ უჭკუო და აგრე რეტი?
მტერი ყოვლი ჩალად გიჩანს, ვინმცა იყო ვითა კეტი,
და ჩემი ლხინი მუნამდის ა, ვირე ვიყო შენი მჭვრეტი!”
stanzas.english_translation: P’hridon humbly did homage, he expressed exceeding gratitude: "O king, why thinkest thou me stupid and thus mazed? Every enemy seems to thee as straw, however much he may be like a thick cudgel. My joy lasts but so long as I shall be a gazer on thee."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1501; Wardrop Stanza 1477): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. სახლსა მისსა მისაღებლად მის ყველასა საჭურჭლისად;
აწ მუნითგან გაემართნეს არაბეთით წავლად გზისად,
და ავთანდილ ა გალეული შესაყრელად, მთვარე, მზისად.
stanzas.english_translation: P’hridon made men go back to bring camels to take away all this treasure to his home. Now they set out thence on the road leading to Arabia. Avt’handil is a minished moon (by longing) to be united with the sun (T’hinat’hin).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1502; Wardrop Stanza 1478): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. დახვდა სოფლები, ციხები, ხშირ-ხშირად თანის-თანები,
მუნ შიგან მყოფსა ემოსა ტანსალურჯი და მწვანები,

stanzas.english_translation: When many days were passed they reached the boundaries of Arabia; they saw villages, castles, frequent, uninterrupted; those dwelling therein had clothed their forms in blue and green, all are bathed in tears for Avt’handil.

stanzas.english_translation: Tariel sent a man to the presence of King Rosten to say: "I venture, O king, to approach thee full of desire; I, King of the Indians, come to your royal court; I will show thee the rosebud, unfaded, unplucked.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1504; Wardrop Stanza 1480): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მაშინ თქვენ ჩემი გეწყინა ნახვა მიწისა შენისა,
ცდა შეპყრობისა ავი ჰქმენ, შემოტევება ცხენისა;
მე შენთა სპათა ვაჩვენე ნიშანი რამე წყენისა,
და დავხოცე მონა მრავალი, მსახურნი სრისა თქვენისა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Formerly my sight of thy ground made you angry; thou didst ill in attempting to capture me, to urge thy horse against me; I showed thine armies some sign of anger, I massacred many slaves, servants of your palace.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1505; Wardrop Stanza 1481): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“აწ ამად მოვალ წინაშე, დავყარენ ჩემნი გზანია,
შემინდოთ, რაცა შეგცოდე, ჰქმნნეთ გაწყრომისა კმანია.
ძღვენი არა მაქვს, მმოწმობენ ფრიდონ და მისნი ყმანია,
და ოდენ ძღვნად თქვენი ავთანდილ მე თქვენთვის მომიტანია”.
stanzas.english_translation: "Now therefore I come before you, I have gone out of my way; you will pardon me that in which I sinned against thee, let thy wrath be sufficient. We have no offerings, as P’hridon and his knights can testify; the only gift I have brought you is your Avt’handil."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1506; Wardrop Stanza 1482): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა მიუვიდა მეფესა მახარობელი ჟამისა,
ვით გაეხარნეს, ვერ იტყვის ენა ერთისა წამისა;
თინათინს ღაწვთა ემატა ელვა შუქისა სამისა,

stanzas.english_translation: Tongue cannot shortly tell how they rejoiced when the messenger of these good tidings came to the king; the brilliancy of three rays was added to T’hinat’hin's cheeks, the shadow of eyebrows and lashes makes fairer the crystal and ruby.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1507; Wardrop Stanza 1483): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ტაბლაკსა ჰკრეს და გაისმა ხმა მაშინ თქართქარებისა.
ლაშქარნი რბოდეს მი-და-მო, ქმნა სწადდა მათკე რებისა.
დაიწყეს მოსხმა ცხენისა, მოღება უნაგრებისა,
და შესხდა სიმრავლე მოყმისა მკლავ-ფიცხელ, გულ-მაგრებისა.
stanzas.english_translation: They beat the kettledrums and peals of joyous laughter were heard, the soldiers ran hither and thither, they desired to run to meet them, they began to lead out the horses and to bring out saddles, a multitude of knights, swift-armed, stout-hearted, mounted.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1508; Wardrop Stanza 1484): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. Tariel sends Asmat ahead and personally intercedes with King Rostevan to pardon Avtandil for his secret departure and bless Avtandil's marriage to Queen Tinatin.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მეფე შეჯდა, გაეგებნეს თავადნი და სრულად სპანი.
ვისცა ესმის, მოვიდიან მას წინაშე სხვაგნით სხვანი.
ყველაკაი ღმერთსა ჰმადლობს, გაამაღლეს მათნი ხმანი,
და თქვეს: “ბოროტსა უმყოფოო, კეთილნია, შენთვის მზანი!”
stanzas.english_translation: The king mounted, the princes and the armies entire go to meet them; whoever hears, others from divers parts come to his presence; all give thanks to God, they raise their voices, they say: "Evil hath no existence; good things (or, the good) are ever ready for thee!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1509; Wardrop Stanza 1485): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა ერთმანერთი აუჩნდა მიგებულ-მოსაგებავთა,
ავთანდილ ეტყვის ტარიელს სიტყვათა დანაზებავთა:
“აგერა ჰხედავთ მინდორთა, მტვერითა შენაღებავთა,
და ამისთვის ვიწვი, სახმილი გულსა ეცხელა, ებავთა.
stanzas.english_translation: When they met and the meeters perceived each other, Avt’handil said with tender words to Tariel: "Behold, seest thou the dust-dyed plains? Therefore a furnace consumes me, my heart is fevered and sad.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1510; Wardrop Stanza 1486): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. Tariel sends Asmat ahead and personally intercedes with King Rostevan to pardon Avtandil for his secret departure and bless Avtandil's marriage to Queen Tinatin.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ისია ჩემი გამზრდელი და თქვენდა მოგებებულა.
იქი ვერ მივალ, მრცხვენიან, გულსა სახმილი დებულა,
ჩემად არაკად სულ-დგმული კაცი არ გაწბილებულა,
და რასაცა მიზამთ, თქვენ იცით, ფრიდონ თქვენდავე ხლებულა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "There is my foster-father; he is come to meet you. I cannot go thither, I am ashamed, a furnace consumes my heart; living man hath never been shamed as I am. What you intend to do for me you know, also P’hridon who is beside you."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1511; Wardrop Stanza 1487): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: Tariel said: "Thou dost well to show respect to thy lord. Now stay, come not thither, stay alone without me. I will go; I will tell the king of thy hiding. With God's help I think I shall soon unite thee to that sun with the figure of an aloe."

მუნ დადგა ლომი ავთანდილ, დაიდგა მცირე კარავი.
ნესტან-დარეჯან მუნვე დგას, იგია მჭვრეტთა მზარავი,

stanzas.english_translation: The lion Avt’handil tarried there; a little tent was put up. Nestan-Daredjan also stayed there, the amazer of beholders; the zephyr of her eyelashes is wafted like a north-east wind. The King of the Indians departed, straight, not secretly.'

stanzas.english_translation: P’hridon went with him; of a truth they were a long time crossing the field. The king knew (of their coming). Tariel went forward alone, his figure swayed; he dismounted and did homage to the bold one strong as a lion; he does honour to the King of the Indians as a father.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1514; Wardrop Stanza 1490): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. ტარიელცა თაყვანი სცა, მივა კოცნად, სასალამოდ;

stanzas.english_translation: Tariel also did homage; he goes to kiss, to greet. The king kissed his neck to give pleasure to his lips; in wonder he speaks, in order to embolden him: "Thou art the sun; separation from thee turns day into night."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1515; Wardrop Stanza 1491): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. გაეკვირვა მეფე მისსა თვალადობა-სიტურფესა,
პირსა უჭვრეტს გაკვირვებით, უქებს მკლავთა სიალფესა;

stanzas.english_translation: The king marvelled at his beauty and good looks, he gazes with wonder on his face, he praises the hardihood of his arms. Then P’hridon also greeted him; he did homage to the king, to the king eager for the sight of Avt’handil.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1516; Wardrop Stanza 1492): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. მეფე ტარიას ქებასა დაჰკრთების, დაეღონების.
ტარიელ ეტყვის: “მეფეო, აწ გული შენ გემონების;
მიკვირს, თუ ეგრე სიკეთე თქვენ ჩემი რად გეგონების!
და რათგან ავთანდილ შენია, სხვა რად ვინ მოგეწონების?
stanzas.english_translation: The king shrinks from praising Taria, and is discouraged. Tariel says: "O king, hereby is my heart subjected to thee; I marvel how you can think thus of my worth; since Avt’handil is thine, how can any other please thee!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1517; Wardrop Stanza 1493): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ნუ გიკვირს მისი ვერ ნახვა და დაყოვნება ხანისა!
მოდი და დავსხდეთ, მეფეო, ამოა კორდი მწვანისა,
გკადრო მიზეზი მისისა თქვენს წინა ვერ მოტანისა,
და ვიაჯ რასამე, აწ მმართებს მოთხოვა მე ფარმანისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "Dost thou not wonder at not seeing him, and at his tarrying! Come and let us sit down, O king, pleasant is this meadow of verdure; I will venture to tell you the reason why I could not bring him before you; I have a favour to ask of you, now I must beg leave of you."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1518; Wardrop Stanza 1494): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
დასხდეს მეფენი, მოადგა გარე სიმრავლე რაზმისა.
ტარიელს პირსა ციმციმი ათქს, უნათლესი ბაზმისა,
ჭვრეტა ახელებს მჭვრეტელთა, ყოფა ქცევისა და ზმისა,
და დაუწყო თხრობა მეფესა სიტყვისა, ბრძნად ნაკაზმისა:
stanzas.english_translation: The kings sat down; the multitude of the host stood round. A smile brighter than a lamps flits over Tariel's face; the sight maddens the beholders of his bearing and gestures. He began to relate to the king a speech wisely chosen:
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1519; Wardrop Stanza 1495): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მეფეო, თავი მემცრობის მე მისად მოსახსენებლად,
მაგრა მოსული თქვენს წინა ვარ შემომხვეწლად მქენებლად.
თვით იგი იაჯს, რომელიც ჩანს მზეებრ შუქთა მფენებლად,
და ვინ არის ჩემად სინათლედ და ჩემად გამათენებლად.
stanzas.english_translation: "O king, I hold myself unworthy to mention this, but I am come before you to entreat, to beg; he himself beseeches who seems a sun-like shedder of rays, he who is my light and enlightener.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1520; Wardrop Stanza 1496): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“აწ ამას გკადრებთ ორნივე ხვეწნით და შემუდარებით,
ავთანდილ დამდვა წამალი მისგან თავისა დადებით,

stanzas.english_translation: "Now we both venture to approach thee with prayer and entreaty. Avt’handil gave me balm befitting him; he forgot that woes quite equal to ours afflicted him. I will not weary thee; a long story is beyond our powers.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1521; Wardrop Stanza 1497): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. “თქვენთა უყვარს ერთმანერთი, ქალი მას და იგი ქალსა,
მით ვიგონებ საბრალოსა, მტირალსა და ფერ-ნამკრთალსა;

და რომე მისცე ქალი თქვენი მკლავ-მაგარსა, გულ-ფიქალსა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Your (children) love each other, the maid loves him and he the maid; therefore I think on him pitiful, tearful and wan, on bended knee I entreat thee, let them no longer be consumed by flame, but give your daughter to the strong-armed, stout-hearted one.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1522; Wardrop Stanza 1498): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ამის მეტსა არას გკადრებ, არ მოკლესა, არცა გრძელსა”.
ამოიღო ხელ-მანდილი, მოინასკვა ზედან ყელსა,
ადგა, მუხლნი მიუყარნა, იაჯების ვითა მზრდელსა,
და გაუკვირდა ყოვლსა კაცსა, მის ამბისა მომსმენელსა.
stanzas.english_translation: "No more than this will I ask of thee, neither short nor long." He drew forth his handkerchief, tied it round his neck, rose up, bent his knee, besought him like a (pupil) before a teacher. It astonished all men who heard this story.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1523; Wardrop Stanza 1499): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. რა ტარიელ მუხლ-მოყრილი ნახა, მეფე შეუზარდა,
შორს უკუდგა, თაყვანის სცა, ქვე მიწამდის დაუვარდა.
მოახსენა: “ხელმწიფეო, ლხინი ყოვლი უკუქარდა,
და თქვენმან აგრე სიმდაბლემან ნახვა თქვენი ჩამადარდა.
stanzas.english_translation: When he saw Tariel on his bended knees, the king was dismayed; he went back a long way, he did homage, he fell down to the earth. He said: "O monarch, all my joy is blown away from me; this abasement of you thus has saddened for me the sight of you.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1524; Wardrop Stanza 1500): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: "How could it be that man should not grant thee whatever thou desirest, or that I should grudge my daughter if thou didst wish (to devote her) to death or slavery even! If you had even ordered it from your home, not even then would my tears flow; none other can she find like him if she fly up even to heaven!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1525; Wardrop Stanza 1501): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. Tariel sends Asmat ahead and personally intercedes with King Rostevan to pardon Avtandil for his secret departure and bless Avtandil's marriage to Queen Tinatin.

stanzas.english_translation: "I could not find a better son-in-law than Avt’handil. Myself I have given the realm to my daughter, she has it and it befits her; the rose blooms anew, my flower is blown. What objection can I make? Only let him be satisfied!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1526; Wardrop Stanza 1502): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. Tariel sends Asmat ahead and personally intercedes with King Rostevan to pardon Avtandil for his secret departure and bless Avtandil's marriage to Queen Tinatin.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“თუ შეგერთო ერთი მონა, თქვენთვის არცა მაშინ მშურდა.
ვინმცა გკადრა შეცილება, უშმაგომცა ვით მოგმდურდა!
თუ ავთანდილ არ მიყვარდა, ასრე მისთვის რად მომსურდა?
და დია, ღმერთო,წინაშე ვარ, ესე ჩემგან დადასტურდა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "If thou wert to marry her to some slave, even then I would not grudge her to thee. Who could refuse thee, how could any save a madman quarrel with thee! If I loved not Avt’handil, why did I thus yearn for him? Verily, O God, I am in Thy presence, this is confirmed by me."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1527; Wardrop Stanza 1503): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. Tariel sends Asmat ahead and personally intercedes with King Rostevan to pardon Avtandil for his secret departure and bless Avtandil's marriage to Queen Tinatin.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა ტარიელ მეფისაგან ესე სიტყვა მოისმინა,
დადრკა, მდაბლად ეთაყვანა, პირსა ზედან დაეფინა.
კვლა მეფემან თაყვანი სცა, წამორევლო, წადგა წინა,
და ერთმანერთი მოიმადლეს, მათ ერთსაცა არ ეწყინა.
stanzas.english_translation: When Tariel heard this speech from the king, he bowed himself, humbly did homage, fell on his face. Then the king did homage to him, he came forward, he stood before him. They thanked each other, nor were they at all annoyed.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1528; Wardrop Stanza 1504): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. ესდენ დიდი სიხარული გაეხარნენ მასცა განა, —
წავიდა და წამოუძღვა, მოიყვანა, მოჰყვა თანა,

stanzas.english_translation: P’hridon mounted, he galloped as herald of good tidings to Avt’handil--indeed, he also rejoiced at this great joy--he went and took him, led him and accompanied him; but he is abashed before the king, darkly he shed (his) beam.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მეფე ადგა,მოეგება; ყმა გარდახდა, რა მივიდა;
ხელთა ჰქონდა ხელმანდილი, პირსა მითა იფარვიდა.
მზე ღრუბელსა მოჰფარვოდა, ქუშდებოდა, ვარდსა ზრვიდა,

stanzas.english_translation: The king arose, met him; the knight dismounted when (the king) came; in his hands he had a handkerchief, therewith he hid his face. The sun was concealed by a cloud, it grew gloomy, the rose was chilled; but how could anything hide his beauty!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1530; Wardrop Stanza 1506): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. Tariel sends Asmat ahead and personally intercedes with King Rostevan to pardon Avtandil for his secret departure and bless Avtandil's marriage to Queen Tinatin.

stanzas.english_translation: The king would have kissed him, tears no longer flow, Avt’handil embraced his feet, the ray streams down; (the king) said: "Arise, be not ashamed, thou has revealed thy prowess; since thou art loyal to me, be not ashamed; why shouldst thou be ashamed before me?"

stanzas.english_translation: He embraced him, he kissed him all over his face; he said: "Thou hast quenched my hot fire, though tardily hast thou appeared to me as water; to her who has herded in the jet and the vicinity (?realm) of the eyelashes to-morrow I shall unite thee, O lion, with the sun, come quickly to her."

stanzas.english_translation: The king embraced the neck of that lion and hero-like one, he seats him close, he speaks to him, kisses him, gazes on his face. That sun so met royalty, as he was worthy of it. Then is joy pleasant, when a man hath passed through grief.

stanzas.english_translation: The knight says to the king: "I marvel that thou speakest of something else, why thou desirest not to see the sun, or why thou delayest! Meet her gaily, conduct her to your house; be clothed in her rays, set them around as a light."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1534; Wardrop Stanza 1510): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: He told Tariel also; they mounted and went to meet the lady. The cheeks of those three Goliaths were dyed to sun colour (i.e., shone like the sun); they met what they desired, they found what they sought; they had handled their swords, not girded them idly on their loins.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1535; Wardrop Stanza 1511): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: Dismounting afar off, the king greeted the lady, the lightning flashing from her cheeks blinded his eyes; she met him, sitting in the palanquin she kissed him. The king began a eulogy; he was wholly bereft of his wits.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1536; Wardrop Stanza 1512): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:

stanzas.english_translation: He said: "O sun, how shall I praise thee, O light, and maker of good weather! For thy sake understandings are mad, and not for nought. O sun-like and moon-like, to what planet do they liken thee! No longer do I wish to look on you, O ye roses and violets!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1537; Wardrop Stanza 1513): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: All they that saw her marvelled at the shedding of her rays. Like a sun she blinded the eyes of the onlookers by the sight of her light; burned by her they found the comfort of their hearts in gazing; wheresoever she appeared crowds came running towards her.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1538; Wardrop Stanza 1514): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
შესხდეს, წავიდეს ყველანი, შინა თავისა მარებად,
ჰქონდეს შვიდნივე მნათობნი მის მზისა დასადარებად,

stanzas.english_translation: They mounted, they all went homewards, they have the seven planets to compare with that sun; her beauty is incomprehensible, it is beyond their understanding. Soon they came to the place of the king's dwelling-house.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1539; Wardrop Stanza 1515): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: They came in, they saw T’hinat’hin, the bestower of woe on them that look on her; the wearing of the purple? beautified the sceptre and crowns bearer; the radiance of her face rested on the faces of the new-comers. The King of the Indians entered, that hero-like sun.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1540; Wardrop Stanza 1516): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: Tariel and his wife humbly saluted the maid, they met, kissed and held pleasant converse, they illumined that house (hall), they made not the light to fade; they turned crystal and ruby into cheeks, jet into eyelashes.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1541; Wardrop Stanza 1517): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: T’hinat’hin invited them up to the lofty royal throne. Tariel said: "Sit thou; it is desired by the Supreme Judge; this day more than all days thy throne befits thee, I seat the lion of lions beside thee the sun of suns."

stanzas.english_translation: Both (? Tariel and Rostevan) took him by the hand and set him on her throne; they placed Avt’handil by the side of her for desire of whom he was slain; she is better than the seen and the unseen, (better) than all sights. stanzas.english_translation: The maiden was bashful and astonished to have Avt’handil seated by her side; her colour paled and her heart shot forth a tremor from within. The king said: "Child, why art thou so bashful before me? the sages say that love in its end will not fail.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“აწ, შვილო, ღმერთმან თქვენ მოგცეს ათას წელ დღეთა გრძელობა,

stanzas.english_translation: "Now, children, God grant you a thousand years’ length of life, happiness, prosperity, glory, and, moreover, freedoms from ills; may heaven not make you fickle, may it fall to your lot to be steadfast like it, may my fate be to have the earth heaped over me by your hands."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1545; Wardrop Stanza 1521): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: Then the king commanded the armies to do homage to Avt’handil: "This is your king," quoth he, "such was God's will. This day he hath my throne, I have old age like an infection. Serve him as well as you have served me, keep my command."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1546; Wardrop Stanza 1522): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: The soldiers and the magnates bent, humbly they did homage; they said: "Let us be as the earth to them that dispose of our lives; them who magnify those of us who are obedient, who liken the disobedient unto corpses, who make the arms of foes to fail (and) encourage our hearts!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 60 ('Going of all Three to the Cave and Thence to Arabia', Stanza 1547; Wardrop Stanza 1523): Part of the narrative sequence in which the three sworn brothers, Nestan-Darejan, and Asmat return to the cave, load the remaining treasures of the Devis, and travel to Arabia. stanzas.english_translation: Tariel too spoke with a eulogy the glorification of hope; he said to the maiden: "You are united, no longer the heat of fires burns thee, thy husband is my brother, I desire too that you be my sister, I will bring to nought those who are false and opposed to thee."

key_maxim_ka: ბოროტსა სძლია კეთილმან, — არსება მისი გრძელია!
key_maxim_en: Good hath overcome evil — its essence is eternal! (Stanza 1363)
